http://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/27922.text: Big News Network.com How can we help you kill more Russians German reporter asks Zelensky FAZ correspondent Michael Martens, whose grandfather was a Wehrmacht officer, posed the question at a press conference held by Zelensky and Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic A German journalist asked Vladimir Zelensky at a press conference in Belgrade how Europeans could help Kiev "kill more Russians," prompting Serbian President AleksandarVucicto raise his eyebrows in apparent disbelief. The provocative question came from Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung correspondent Michael Martens during a joint press conference following Zelensky's talks with Vucic on Saturday. "Can you tell us Europeans what can we concretely do to help you to kill more Russians?" Martens asked. He hastily added he meant "more Russian soldiers, of course," before asking whether the two leaders had discussed military cooperation. Footage shows Vucic raising his eyebrows in apparent disbelief as he hears the question. width="560" height="315" src="https://mf.b37mrtl.ru/files/2026.08/6a7853a9203027441660bc89.mp4" frameborder="0" > Clips of the exchange quickly went viral on social media, triggering a wave of angry reactions. Some users denounced the wording as offensive and accused Martens of "incitement to hatred." Others branded him a "Nazi," noting that his grandfather served as an officer on a Wehrmacht command staff during World War II - a fact that Martens himself hasacknowledged. Martens laterdoubled downon X, insisting there was nothing "scandalous" or "shocking" about his wording and expressing surprise at the backlash. "It is not scandalous to ask the Ukrainian President how Europe can help Ukraine to kill more Russians. That is what is needed," he wrote. "Outside Barbieworld, this is how wars are fought." Although Martens' question was directed at Zelensky, Vucic answered first. "We did not discuss military cooperation today," the Serbian president said. "What happens when the war ends is another matter. And speaking about killing, I hope all killing will end." Zelensky, meanwhile, used the question to reiterate his demands that Kiev's Western backers send more money and slap more sanctions on Moscow. Serbia remains one of the few European countries to maintain close ties with Moscow since the Ukraine conflict escalated in 2022. As an EU candidate state, however, it has faced pressure from Brussels to distance itself from Russia. Last month, Vucic accused the EU of trying to "govern Serbia by email" and dictate its foreign relations. Ahead of his meeting with Zelensky, he reiterated that Belgrade will follow its own course and not join sanctions against Russia. Martens' question comes amid growingRussophobiain the West, ranging from anti-Russianrhetoricby politicians, journalists and other public figures to restrictions on Russian media, culture, and language and the destruction of Soviet memorials. Just this week, Polish President Karol Nawrocki made his own remarks about killing Russians, telling a rally in Warsaw that helping Ukraine do so was in Poland's strategic interest. "Wherever the Moskal is being fought, Poland helps," he said, using a historic derogatory term for Russians. Commenting on the remark, Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova called such outbursts "clinical Russophobia," while lamenting that this had become "the norm" for many in the West. https://www.thenational.scot/news/world/.text: COMMENT Russia Ukraine Relief War in Ukraine Military Vladmir Putin makes a desert for himself and apologists call it peace By Findlay Young, convenor, SNP Ukraine Solidarity Caucus Share 0 Comments 3 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. IN his article, Vladimir Unkovski-Korica attempts to argue that neither he nor Stop the War are pro-Putin. He calls this a smear. He claims that Stop the War “opposed Russia’s invasion from the outset”. This, reader, is simply not true. In my original piece, I quoted an article published on the Stop the War website on March 23, 2014, written by Eamonn McCann, titled: “In game of Great Power politics, if we have to pick a side over Crimea, let it be Russia.” The title speaks for itself. Stop the War was and is an affirmatively pro-Putin organisation. The offending article is still up on Stop the War’s website. However, the title has been changed to: “Neither Washington nor Moscow has had genuine concern for the interests of any section of the Ukrainian people.” This behaviour is revealing. Stop the War are apologists for Vladimir Putin, and revisionists. Another article published on the Stop the War website, this time on February, 11, 2022, was titled “US-Nato Militarism is the Cause, Not the Solution”. This is another classic trope of pro-Putin propaganda that seeks to deflect blame for the invasion away from the invaders. Image from Ukraine following a Russian strike (Image: AP/Oleksandr Ratushniak) Unkovski-Korica is guilty of this himself, calling Ukrainian resistance to Russia’s invasion a “proxy war between Nato and Russia”. He does this to hand-wave away the inconvenient fact that it is Ukrainians fighting this war, and not the West; that Ukrainians want to resist Russia, and they want our support to do it. They didn’t want the so-called “peace deal” offered in 2022, which would have meant allowing the occupation of millions of Ukrainians. Putin’s position has not changed; he still demands territory his forces have not been able to seize in four years of fighting as a precondition to peace. Ukrainians are still not willing to accept that. Unkovski-Korica refers to Stop the War’s opposition to the invasion of Iraq. In doing so he unintentionally illustrates how far Stop the War has fallen. Iraq was an imperialist invasion launched by ourselves and our allies. When Stop the War opposed it in the early 2000s, they were in step with huge swathes of the general public and most of the trade unions in this country. Now, with Ukraine , Stop the War argues against opposing an invasion. By doing so, it places itself far out on the political fringe, alongside George Galloway, members of the Socialist Workers’ Party, Reform UK and, latterly, Donald Trump . Most of the British trade unions stand firm in solidarity with the KVPU and FPU, Ukraine’s two largest trade union federations, who both advocate continued resistance to Russia’s invasion. READ MORE: Emergency crews leave Cairngorms wildfire site five weeks after blaze started Unkovski-Korica claims Putin’s Russia is not like Hitler’s Germany, and therefore coercing Ukraine into allowing the annexation of their territory is not akin to the Allies’ betrayal of Czechoslovakia. He claims Putin’s Russia is authoritarian and aggressive, but not fascist. He talks about GDP, and industrialisation. This probably makes sense in an obscure political reading group in the West End of Glasgow; I suspect the difference means very little to the men, women, and children who may be huddling in bomb shelters and underground stations in Kyiv tonight. Unkovski-Korica wheels out another well-established piece of propaganda designed to erode support for Ukraine, to Putin’s benefit: the notion that Zelenskyy’s government has allied itself to Benjamin Netanyahu ’s Israel. This does not have basis in reality. Yes, Zelenskyy, like many other leaders, expressed solidarity with Israel in the immediate aftermath of the October 7 attacks. That very quickly changed once Israel’s intentions in Gaza became clear. On October 18, 2023, Ukraine’s foreign ministry condemned the civilian casualties from Israel’s attack on Al Ahli Hospital, reiterating their support for a two-state solution. On July 18, 2024, Ukraine sent 1000 tonnes of wheat flour to the Palestinian territories. Throughout this, Ukraine continued to recognise Palestinian statehood. Since then, Israeli-Ukrainian relations have been difficult at best. Last April, Israel ignored Ukraine’s request to seize a Russian ship accused of carrying grain from occupied Ukraine. Worth noting is that in the 2024/25 season, Russia supplied 89% of Israel’s wheat. Between November 2023 and October 2025, Russia supplied 45% of Israel’s petroleum. These exports have now ceased thanks to Ukrainian strikes on Russia’s oil refineries. Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy (Image: AP) However, there is more to Ukraine than Zelenskyy and his government. There is plenty of grassroots solidarity with Palestine amongst ordinary Ukrainians. Andriy Movchan and Nina Potarska both joined the Global Sumud Flotilla under the slogan: “From Ukraine to Palestine, occupation is a crime!” It is a slogan I take to heart. I firmly believe that occupation is a crime, from Ukraine to Palestine. Unkovski-Korica, evidently, does not agree. He calls this stance “moralism”. Well, of course it’s moralistic! What decent human being can look at the ruins of Gaza or Mariupol and come away thinking that the victims must make further compromises with the perpetrators? What “negotiated settlement” does Unkovski-Korica think the people of Palestine must make with Netanyahu? I advocate solidarity with the people of Ukraine in their war of national liberation because, as a Scottish nationalist, I apply my principles of anti-imperialism and national self-determination uniformly. Unkovski-Korica and Stop the War argue that our solidarity should extend only occasionally; to the victims of some imperialist nations, and not others. Those who advocate for Ukraine’s capitulation very evidently do not care about ordinary Ukrainians. READ MORE: BBC responds to anger over documentary 'showing Glasgow as backwater of drunks' They do not care that ordinary Ukrainians are not willing to accept any terms that Putin has thus far been willing to offer. They do not care about the pain and suffering that would be inflicted if we were to walk away from Ukraine now. I would challenge them to come up with a single convincing reason why we should not agree to Ukraine’s requests for air-defence interceptors to stop Russia’s ballistic missile strikes. They do not care about those massacred at Bucha. Or the theatre full of children bombed at Mariupol. They do not care about the Crimean Tatar activists disappeared by Russian security services, or the queer Ukrainians under occupation, who face total annihilation. They do not care about the mass graves, or the torture chambers, or the filtration camps. These people do not want a fair and just peace for Ukraine. They want Ukrainians to die quietly, under the living death that is colonial occupation. Russia makes a desert and Putin’s apologists call it “peace”. What peace should be negotiated with people responsible for these atrocities? If it was our own country under occupation, our own children murdered, our own friends and family raped and brutalised, we might be entitled to an opinion. But it is not our country. Not mine, or Unkovski-Korica’s, or (most likely) yours, reader. Ukraine belongs to its people. How and when they negotiate an end to this conflict is their business , not ours. What is our business is how we carry ourselves, how we apply our principles. My principles tell me that my desire for my country’s freedom means I should desire it for other countries as well. For that reason, I say Slava Ukraini, and Alba gu bràth. Russia Ukraine Relief War in Ukraine Military Share 0 Comments Get involved with the news Send your news & photos Loading... https://www.dw.com/en/hamburg-court-jail.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OHG3 The men were sentenced in Hamburg after being extradited from Denmark [FILE: October 3, 2020] Image: xim.gs/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement A Hamburg court on Thursday sentenced two men accused of plotting to target Jewish leaders in Germany on behalf of Iran's secret service to multiple years in prison. Both were found guilty of espionage and attempted murder. One defendant was given a four-and-a-half year sentence, while the other received an eight-and-a-half year sentence as the mastermind of the planned attacks. Prosecutors said that one defendant, a 54-year-old Dane with Afghan roots, had received his orders directly from Iran's al-Quds Brigades, the foreign arm of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps. The man was said to have recruited his accomplice, a 43-year-old Afghan man living in Denmark, to carry out one of the attacks, or find someone who could. The 43-year-old was also tasked with finding a weapon with which to carry out one of the attacks. Beyond targeting two high-profile individuals, the 54-year-old had reportedly made preparations for an arson attack on a kosher deli in Berlin. The defendants were arrested by Danish authorities in the city of Aarhus last year and extradited to Germany. How Europe, the US can better protect Jewish communities To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Who were convicted defendants planning to attack? Among the figures the pair planned to attack was Josef Schuster , the president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, the court found. Another prospective target was Green Party politician Volker Beck, president of the German-Israeli society. Beck called on Berlin to expel Iran's ambassador and consular officials after charges against the men were made public. "Jewish life and a commitment to the Jewish and democratic state are repeatedly threatened with murder and attacked by the regime of the Islamic Republic of Iran on German soil," he said. Germany's Foreign Office summoned Iran's ambassador after Danish authorities made the arrests, prompting the Iranian embassy in Berlin to release a statement rejecting what it called "unfounded allegations made at the behest of Iran's enemies."
